events.reason: Cross-polarized return over vegetation fell 2.7 dB and stayed low, a sign that leaves and branches are gone; the patch grew over 5 passes, the way a fire spreads.
events.title: Burned area near Niebla and Doñana, Huelva
events.summary: The radar first saw signs of burned vegetation near Niebla and the edge of Doñana on 14 August 2026, and the scarred area grew over five satellite passes to about 372 square kilometres by 6 November 2026. The land was mostly trees and shrubs, and the radar signal from leaves and branches dropped and stayed low, which is what a fire scar typically looks like. The burned area was no longer growing at the latest pass, has not yet recovered, and the detection is fairly confident (83%).

events.title: Crops filling in near Niebla and Doñana, Huelva
events.summary: The radar saw about 4.2 square kilometres of mostly farmland near Niebla and the edge of Doñana grow steadily brighter from 14 August 2026, peaking on 26 August and staying bright across eight passes, which is how growing crops usually look from orbit. By the latest pass on 6 November the change was fading but had not yet returned to normal. Confidence is moderate (about 63%), and although this site is tracked as the Huelva wildfire, the radar did not link this change to fire.

events.title: Crops filling in near Niebla, Huelva
events.summary: Farmland on the edge of Doñana near Niebla, Huelva, began looking different to the satellite on 14 August 2026 in a way that matches crops growing and filling in, reaching its largest extent of about 1.5 km² on 26 August. The change has held steady through the latest pass on 6 November 2026 and has not returned to its earlier state. The detection is fairly confident (83%), and the area is almost entirely cropland with some grass.

events.title: Likely burn scar near Niebla and Doñana edge
events.summary: The radar detected a loss of trees, shrubs and grass near Niebla on the edge of Doñana, Huelva, consistent with a fire scar. The scar was first seen on 19 September 2026, grew over three satellite passes and reached about 1.41 km² by 25 October. On the latest pass, 6 November, the changed area was shrinking but had not returned to normal; confidence in this detection is moderate, about 77%.
